blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Singhs, thus, continued bearing hardships cheerfully, As they continued living in their country amidst suffering. Getting together occasionally whenever possible, They would plunder and crush the (alien) claimants to power. (1)
lines: The Singhs, thus, continued bearing hardships cheerfully,
As they continued living in their country amidst suffering.
Getting together occasionally whenever possible,
They would plunder and crush the (alien) claimants to power.

blocks.text: They would roam fearlessly like lions at night, While going into hibernation during the day. They, having no scare of the host of enemy troops, Even a few Singhs would attack the enemy at night. (2)
lines: They would roam fearlessly like lions at night,
While going into hibernation during the day.
They, having no scare of the host of enemy troops,
Even a few Singhs would attack the enemy at night.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Wherever the Mughal troops put up a camp, The Singhs would reach there as night. Sneaking into their camp furtively like a thief, They would loot and rob the enemy camp. (3)
lines: Wherever the Mughal troops put up a camp,
The Singhs would reach there as night.
Sneaking into their camp furtively like a thief,
They would loot and rob the enemy camp.

blocks.text: Episode About Singhs' occupation of a Lion's Cave (The Way the Singhs lived in a Lion's Cave)
Dohra:

(Dear readers) listen to the episode about those Singhs, Who had to remain confined perforce in a Lion's cave. Listen to the names of those (brave) Singhs, Who defied the Mughals even when confined underground. (1)
lines: (Dear readers) listen to the episode about those Singhs,
Who had to remain confined perforce in a Lion's cave.
Listen to the names of those (brave) Singhs,
Who defied the Mughals even when confined underground.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Mirankot which is my (author's) native place, There lived a Singh by the name of S. Laddha Singh. Being my father's elder brother of a (Jat Sikh) sub-caste Bhangoo, He underwent a lot of harassment in a foreign territory. (2)
lines: Mirankot which is my (author's) native place,
There lived a Singh by the name of S.
Laddha Singh.
Being my father's elder brother of a (Jat Sikh) sub-caste Bhangoo,
He underwent a lot of harassment in a foreign territory.

blocks.text: Neither were the Singhs given any financial assistance on credit, Nor did any villager provide them shelter, suspecting them to be burglars. As the (homeless) Singhs took shelter in the waste lands, They were branded as highwaymen and low caste nomads. (3)
lines: Neither were the Singhs given any financial assistance on credit,
Nor did any villager provide them shelter, suspecting them to be burglars.
As the (homeless) Singhs took shelter in the waste lands,
They were branded as highwaymen and low caste nomads.

blocks.text: Country people coming in hot pursuit would capture them, Thereafter starving them by withholding every kind of food. So, being harassed, the Singhs would leave for distant lands, But some of them, being fed up with maltreatment, would return home. (4)
lines: Country people coming in hot pursuit would capture them,
Thereafter starving them by withholding every kind of food.
So, being harassed, the Singhs would leave for distant lands,
But some of them, being fed up with maltreatment, would return home.

blocks.text: Being harassed abroad, they would return home, To pass time seeking shelter incognito here and there. Spotting out an underground lions' (empty) cave, They widened it from inside by digging out some earth. (5)
lines: Being harassed abroad, they would return home,
To pass time seeking shelter incognito here and there.
Spotting out an underground lions' (empty) cave,
They widened it from inside by digging out some earth.

blocks.text: Dohra:
They would come out of the cave at night, While remaining in hiding during the day. These (fugitive) Singhs, thus, adopted a way of life, As is the natural mode of life of the owl species. (6)
lines: They would come out of the cave at night,
While remaining in hiding during the day.
These (fugitive) Singhs, thus, adopted a way of life,
As is the natural mode of life of the owl species.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
A Singh would leave the cave very night, And all of them would eat whatever he brought from home.
If another Singh happened to join them inside the cave, They would feed him first before feeding themselves. (7)
lines: If another Singh happened to join them inside the cave,
They would feed him first before feeding themselves.

blocks.text: If a Singh were found to be without provisions, They would feed him even if they themselves went without food. Those who were more enterprising among these Singhs, They would run out in a group (to fetch provisions). (8)
lines: If a Singh were found to be without provisions,
They would feed him even if they themselves went without food.
Those who were more enterprising among these Singhs,
They would run out in a group (to fetch provisions).

blocks.text: Laying their hands on some grains and vegetables, They would, sustain themselves through means fair and foul. Only a rare among them having prosperous parents, Would go home at night to feed himself well. (9)
lines: Laying their hands on some grains and vegetables,
They would, sustain themselves through means fair and foul.
Only a rare among them having prosperous parents,
Would go home at night to feed himself well.

blocks.text: Dohra:
As these Singhs were, thus, passing their days, In the shelter of an underground lion's cave. A state spy, spotting out their hideout, Informed the Mughal authorities of their location. (10)
lines: As these Singhs were, thus, passing their days,
In the shelter of an underground lion's cave.
A state spy, spotting out their hideout,
Informed the Mughal authorities of their location.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Getting this information, Mughal troops arrived there, Camouflaging themselves on one side of the cave. The moment they spotted the Singhs entering the cave, There were only three Singhs at that moment. (11)
lines: Getting this information,
Mughal troops arrived there,
Camouflaging themselves on one side of the cave.
The moment they spotted the Singhs entering the cave,
There were only three Singhs at that moment.

blocks.text: While Laddha Singh Bhangoo was one as mentioned earlier, Ram Singh was another from Lambay Hayher village. The third Singh being Sulakhan Singh Gill, These three were spotted by the Mughals entering the cave. (12)
lines: While Laddha Singh Bhangoo was one as mentioned earlier,
Ram Singh was another from Lambay Hayher village.
The third Singh being Sulakhan Singh Gill,
These three were spotted by the Mughals entering the cave.

blocks.text: As the Mughal soldiers rushed to attack them, These Singhs went underground hurling defiance. Wielding their swords and daggers they took positions. In order to have it out with the besieged Singhs. (13)
lines: As the Mughal soldiers rushed to attack them,
These Singhs went underground hurling defiance.
Wielding their swords and daggers they took positions.
In order to have it out with the besieged Singhs.

blocks.text: The Singhs had provisions which could last for a day or two, Though they had water that was available from underground. When the Mughals failed in their attempt to dig them out, They resolved to adopt an other strategy to deal with them. (14)
lines: The Singhs had provisions which could last for a day or two,
Though they had water that was available from underground.
When the Mughals failed in their attempt to dig them out,
They resolved to adopt an other strategy to deal with them.

blocks.text: Dohra:

They should fire such a volley of bullets into the cave, That there should be a lot of smoke and suffocation inside. When the Singhs fainted and became unconscious with smoke, They should be killed after dragging them out. (15)
lines: They should fire such a volley of bullets into the cave,
That there should be a lot of smoke and suffocation inside.
When the Singhs fainted and became unconscious with smoke,
They should be killed after dragging them out.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Putting the muzzles of all their muskets in the cave's opening, The Mughals let out a volley of bullets inside the cave. As the cave got filled with dense smoke and darkness, The Singhs felt choked with smoke and lack of air. (16)
lines: Putting the muzzles of all their muskets in the cave's opening,
The Mughals let out a volley of bullets inside the cave.
As the cave got filled with dense smoke and darkness,
The Singhs felt choked with smoke and lack of air.

blocks.text: As the Singhs felt extremely tortured inside the cave, They made attempts to block the entry of smoke. Whatever articles of clothing they had with them, They corked the cave's opening with those clothes. (17)
lines: As the Singhs felt extremely tortured inside the cave,
They made attempts to block the entry of smoke.
Whatever articles of clothing they had with them,
They corked the cave's opening with those clothes.

blocks.text: Then, the Mughals, thinking of another strategy, Thought of forcing the people to dig out the whole cave. Deciding on such a strategy and sending their troops, The Mughals brought the people with spades in their hands. (18)
lines: Then, the Mughals, thinking of another strategy,
Thought of forcing the people to dig out the whole cave.
Deciding on such a strategy and sending their troops,
The Mughals brought the people with spades in their hands.

blocks.text: People, being quite clever, came with the troops, And they were also made to dig the caves with the spades. But they struck the spades so oddly that the spades got dismantled, For which lapse they were roughed up by the Mughal soldiers. (19)
lines: People, being quite clever, came with the troops,
And they were also made to dig the caves with the spades.
But they struck the spades so oddly that the spades got dismantled,
For which lapse they were roughed up by the Mughal soldiers.

blocks.text: Dohra:
As the soldiers went out to call the carpenters, For fixing the dismantled spades in to the handles, The darkness descended on the scene, And the troops returned to their barracks. (20)
lines: As the soldiers went out to call the carpenters,
For fixing the dismantled spades in to the handles,
The darkness descended on the scene,
And the troops returned to their barracks.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, the Mughal soldiers adopting another tactic, Set the Cave's opening on fire after filling it with wooden logs. As the raging fire burnt the corked clothings, The Singhs inside underwent a lot of torture. (21)
lines: Thereafter, the Mughal soldiers adopting another tactic,
Set the Cave's opening on fire after filling it with wooden logs.
As the raging fire burnt the corked clothings,
The Singhs inside underwent a lot of torture.

blocks.text: Then the Singhs made one more attempt, And plugged the opening with a moistened clay batter. As they attempted to save their lives somehow, Darkness descended on the scene once again. (22)
lines: Then the Singhs made one more attempt,
And plugged the opening with a moistened clay batter.
As they attempted to save their lives somehow,
Darkness descended on the scene once again.

blocks.text: The people (in the meanwhile) frightened the Mughals, That other Singhs would definitely attack them at night. As the Mughals deserted the place being scared, The people gathered around the cave from all sides. (23)
lines: The people (in the meanwhile) frightened the Mughals,
That other Singhs would definitely attack them at night.
As the Mughals deserted the place being scared,
The people gathered around the cave from all sides.

blocks.text: They brought the Singhs out after putting out the fire, Such being the ordeal through which the Singhs passed. I (the author) having heard from those who faced it, Have narrated it after a thorough contemplation. (24)
lines: They brought the Singhs out after putting out the fire,
Such being the ordeal through which the Singhs passed.
I (the author) having heard from those who faced it,
Have narrated it after a thorough contemplation.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Although the Singhs underwent such unspeakable ordeals, They did not give up their claim to sovereignty. It is for these sacrifices that sovereignty was conferred, On their commonwealth of Kshtryas, Artisans, wine traders and Jats. (25)
lines: Although the Singhs underwent such unspeakable ordeals,
They did not give up their claim to sovereignty.
It is for these sacrifices that sovereignty was conferred,
On their commonwealth of Kshtryas,
Artisans, wine traders and Jats.
